parts.text: Can she trust touch alone to say whether the tap water is hot or cold?

options.text: No, because each hand may judge the same tap water differently after iced juice and warm soup.
Yes, because touch always gives the true temperature of tap water.
Yes, but only for the hand that was in the warm soup.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Nidhi holds her left hand in a glass of iced juice and her right hand in a bowl of warm soup. Then she puts both hands into the same basin of tap water.

part_answers.answer: Touch depends on what each hand felt before, so the same tap water can feel different; temperature needs a thermometer check.

teacher.key_rationale: After opposite warm and cold exposures, touch can mislead about the same water. A measured temperature is needed for a reliable hot-or-cold judgement.
